rows.subtopic: Mode of Grouped Data
rows.stem: The mode of a grouped frequency distribution is 75 and the modal class is 65-80. The frequency of the class preceding the modal class is 6 and the frequency of the class succeeding the modal class is 8. Find the frequency of the modal class.
rows.solution:
Mode \(= 75\) and the modal class is 65 to 80, so \(l = 65\), \(h = 15\), \(f_0 = 6\), \(f_2 = 8\). Let the frequency of the modal class be \(f_1\).

\(\text{Mode} = l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h\)

\(75 = 65 + \dfrac{f_1 - 6}{2f_1 - 6 - 8} \times 15\), so \(10 = \dfrac{15(f_1 - 6)}{2f_1 - 14}\).

Dividing by 5 and cross-multiplying: \(2(2f_1 - 14) = 3(f_1 - 6)\), that is \(4f_1 - 28 = 3f_1 - 18\), so \(f_1 = 10\).

The frequency of the modal class is 10.

rows.subtopic: nth Term of an AP
rows.stem: How many natural numbers are there between 1 and 1000 which are divisible by 5 but not by 2 ?
rows.solution:
A number divisible by 5 but not by 2 is an odd multiple of 5. Between 1 and 1000 these are 5, 15, 25, 35, ..., 995.

They form an AP with \(a = 5\), \(d = 10\) and last term \(a_n = 995\).

\(a + (n - 1)d = 995\), so \(5 + (n - 1)10 = 995\), \((n - 1)10 = 990\), \(n - 1 = 99\) and \(n = 100\).

There are 100 such natural numbers.

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: If the sum of the roots of the quadratic equation \(ky^2 - 11y + (k - 23) = 0\) is \(\dfrac{13}{21}\) more than the product of the roots, then find the value of k.
rows.solution:
For \(ky^2 - 11y + (k - 23) = 0\), \(a = k\), \(b = -11\), \(c = k - 23\).

Sum of roots \(= -\dfrac{b}{a} = \dfrac{11}{k}\) and product of roots \(= \dfrac{c}{a} = \dfrac{k - 23}{k}\).

The sum is \(\dfrac{13}{21}\) more than the product:

\(\dfrac{11}{k} = \dfrac{k - 23}{k} + \dfrac{13}{21}\), so \(\dfrac{11 - (k - 23)}{k} = \dfrac{13}{21}\), that is \(\dfrac{34 - k}{k} = \dfrac{13}{21}\).

\(21(34 - k) = 13k\), so \(714 = 34k\) and \(k = 21\).

Check: with \(k = 21\) the equation is \(21y^2 - 11y - 2 = 0\); the sum of roots is \(\dfrac{11}{21}\), the product is \(-\dfrac{2}{21}\), and the difference is \(\dfrac{13}{21}\).

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: If \(x = -2\) is the common solution of quadratic equations \(ax^2 + x - 3a = 0\) and \(x^2 + bx + b = 0\), then find the value of \(a^2b\).
rows.solution:
Since \(x = -2\) is a root of both equations, it satisfies each of them.

In \(ax^2 + x - 3a = 0\): \(a(-2)^2 + (-2) - 3a = 0\), so \(4a - 2 - 3a = 0\) and \(a = 2\).

In \(x^2 + bx + b = 0\): \((-2)^2 + b(-2) + b = 0\), so \(4 - 2b + b = 0\) and \(b = 4\).

So \(a^2b = 2^2 \times 4 = 16\).

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: In Fig. 1, there are two concentric circles with centre O. If ARC and AQB are tangents to the smaller circle from the point A lying on the larger circle, find the length of AC, if AQ = 5 cm.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the roles of the points Q, R and C named in the stem are fixed only by Fig. 1. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
AQ and AR are the two tangents from the external point A to the smaller circle, so \(AR = AQ = 5\) cm.

Join OR. The radius OR is perpendicular to the tangent at R, so \(OR \perp AC\).

AC is a chord of the larger circle, and the perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it. So R is the mid-point of AC and \(RC = AR = 5\) cm.

\(AC = AR + RC = 5 + 5 = 10\) cm.

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 176 sq cm and its volume is 1232 cu cm. What is the height of the cylinder ?
rows.solution:
Let r be the radius and h the height of the cylinder.

Curved surface area: \(2\pi rh = 176\) ... (i)

Volume: \(\pi r^2 h = 1232\) ... (ii)

Dividing (ii) by (i): \(\dfrac{\pi r^2 h}{2\pi rh} = \dfrac{1232}{176}\), so \(\dfrac{r}{2} = 7\) and \(r = 14\) cm.

From (i): \(2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14 \times h = 176\), so \(88h = 176\) and \(h = 2\) cm.

The height of the cylinder is 2 cm.

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: The largest sphere is carved out of a solid cube of side 21 cm. Find the volume of the sphere.
rows.solution:
The largest sphere that fits in a cube touches all six faces, so its diameter equals the side of the cube: 21 cm. Its radius is \(r = \dfrac{21}{2}\) cm.

\(\text{Volume} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{21}{2} \times \dfrac{21}{2} \times \dfrac{21}{2} = 4851\ \text{cm}^3\).

The volume of the sphere is \(4851\ \text{cm}^3\).

rows.subtopic: Construction of Tangents to a Circle
rows.stem: Construct a pair of tangents to a circle of radius 4 cm which are inclined to each other at an angle of \(60^\circ\).
rows.solution:
The tangents at the ends of two radii OA and OB meet at P, and \(\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ\). In the quadrilateral OAPB the angles add to \(360^\circ\), so for \(\angle APB = 60^\circ\) the radii must make \(\angle AOB = 360^\circ - 90^\circ - 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\).

Steps of construction:

1. Draw a circle with centre O and radius 4 cm.

2. Draw any radius OA.

3. At O, construct \(\angle AOB = 120^\circ\), with B on the circle.

4. At A, construct a line perpendicular to OA, and at B, construct a line perpendicular to OB.

5. Let these two perpendiculars meet at P.

PA and PB are the required tangents, inclined to each other at \(60^\circ\).

Justification: PA is perpendicular to the radius OA at its end A on the circle, so PA is a tangent; likewise PB is a tangent. In quadrilateral OAPB, \(\angle APB = 360^\circ - 90^\circ - 90^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ\).

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: Had Aarush scored 8 more marks in a Mathematics test, out of 35 marks, 7 times these marks would have been 4 less than square of his actual marks. How many marks did he get in the test ?
rows.solution:
Let Aarush's actual marks be x. With 8 more marks he would have \(x + 8\), and 7 times that is 4 less than \(x^2\):

\(7(x + 8) = x^2 - 4\)

\(x^2 - 7x - 60 = 0\)

\(x^2 - 12x + 5x - 60 = 0\), so \((x - 12)(x + 5) = 0\).

So \(x = 12\) or \(x = -5\). Marks cannot be negative, so \(x = 12\).

Aarush got 12 marks in the test.

Check: \(7 \times 20 = 140\) and \(12^2 - 4 = 140\).

rows.subtopic: Angle of Elevation Problems
rows.stem: An aeroplane when flying at a height of 3125 m from the ground passes vertically below another plane at an instant when the angles of elevation of the two planes from the same point on the ground are \(30^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) respectively. Find the distance between the two planes at that instant.
rows.solution:
Let A be the point on the ground, B the point on the ground vertically below the planes, C the lower plane and D the upper plane. Then \(BC = 3125\) m, and let \(CD = x\) and \(AB = y\). The angles of elevation are \(\angle BAC = 30^\circ\) and \(\angle BAD = 60^\circ\).

In right triangle ABC: \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{BC}{AB}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3125}{y}\) and \(y = 3125\sqrt{3}\) m.

In right triangle ABD: \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{BD}{AB} = \dfrac{x + 3125}{y}\), so \(\sqrt{3}\,y = x + 3125\).

\(\sqrt{3} \times 3125\sqrt{3} = x + 3125\), so \(9375 = x + 3125\) and \(x = 6250\).

The distance between the two planes at that instant is 6250 m.

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: If the last term of an A.P. of 30 terms is 119 and the \(8^{\text{th}}\) term from the end (towards the first term) is 91, then find the common difference of the A.P. Hence, find the sum of all the terms of the A.P.
rows.solution:
Let the first term be a and the common difference d.

The last (30th) term is 119: \(a + 29d = 119\) ... (i)

The 8th term from the end is the \((30 - 8 + 1) = 23\)rd term from the beginning: \(a + 22d = 91\) ... (ii)

Subtracting (ii) from (i): \(7d = 28\), so \(d = 4\). Then \(a = 91 - 88 = 3\).

The common difference is 4.

\(S_{30} = \dfrac{n}{2}(a + l) = \dfrac{30}{2}(3 + 119) = 15 \times 122 = 1830\).

The sum of all the terms is 1830.

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: In Fig.-2, if a circle touches the side QR of \(\Delta PQR\) at S and extended sides PQ and PR at M and N, respectively, then prove that \(PM = \dfrac{1}{2}(PQ + QR + PR)\)
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - Fig. 2 draws the triangle PQR and the circle the stem describes; nothing needed is only in the drawing. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length. So:

from Q: \(QS = QM\); from R: \(RS = RN\); from P: \(PM = PN\).

M lies on PQ produced beyond Q, so \(PM = PQ + QM\); N lies on PR produced beyond R, so \(PN = PR + RN\).

\(2PM = PM + PN\)

\(= (PQ + QM) + (PR + RN)\)

\(= PQ + QS + PR + RS\)

\(= PQ + (QS + RS) + PR\)

\(= PQ + QR + PR\), since S lies on QR.

So \(PM = \dfrac{1}{2}(PQ + QR + PR)\).

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: In Fig. 3, a triangle ABC is drawn to circumscribe a circle of radius 4 cm such that the segments BD and DC into which BC is divided by the point of contact D are of lengths 6 cm and 8 cm respectively. If the area of \(\Delta ABC\) is \(84 \text{ cm}^2\), find the lengths of sides AB and AC.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - Fig. 3 draws the triangle and incircle the stem describes and repeats its lengths; nothing needed is only in the drawing. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
Let the circle touch AB at F and AC at E. Tangents from an external point are equal, so:

\(BF = BD = 6\) cm, \(CE = CD = 8\) cm, and let \(AF = AE = x\) cm.

Then \(AB = (x + 6)\) cm, \(AC = (x + 8)\) cm and \(BC = 14\) cm.

Join O to A, B and C. The radius to each point of contact is perpendicular to that side, so each of triangles OBC, OCA and OAB has height 4 cm, and

\(\text{ar}(ABC) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times (AB + BC + CA) = 2(x + 6 + 14 + x + 8) = 2(2x + 28) = 4x + 56\).

\(4x + 56 = 84\), so \(4x = 28\) and \(x = 7\).

So \(AB = 7 + 6 = 13\) cm and \(AC = 7 + 8 = 15\) cm.

Check by Heron's formula: the sides are 13, 14, 15, so \(s = 21\) and the area is \(\sqrt{21 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6} = \sqrt{7056} = 84\ \text{cm}^2\).

rows.subtopic: Angle of Elevation Problems
rows.stem: From the top of an 8 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is \(60^\circ\) and the angle of depression of its foot is \(45^\circ\). Determine the height of the tower. (Take \(\sqrt{3} = 1.732\)).
rows.solution:
Let AB be the building, \(AB = 8\) m, and CD the tower of height h m, with A and C on the ground. Draw BE parallel to AC, meeting CD at E, so ABEC is a rectangle: \(CE = AB = 8\) m and \(BE = AC\).

The angle of depression of the foot C from B is \(45^\circ\), so \(\angle ACB = 45^\circ\). In right triangle BAC, \(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{AC}\), so \(1 = \dfrac{8}{AC}\) and \(AC = 8\) m. So \(BE = 8\) m.

The angle of elevation of the top D from B is \(60^\circ\). In right triangle BED, \(DE = h - 8\) and \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{DE}{BE}\):

\(\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{h - 8}{8}\), so \(h = 8\sqrt{3} + 8 = 8(\sqrt{3} + 1)\).

\(h = 8(1.732 + 1) = 8 \times 2.732 = 21.856\) m.

The height of the tower is 21.856 m.

rows.subtopic: Median of Grouped Data
rows.stem: Find the median age of people enrolled for the camp.
rows.context:
Yoga is an ancient practice which is a form of meditation and exercise. By practising yoga, we not even make our body healthy but also achieve inner peace and calmness. The International Yoga Day is celebrated on \(21^{\text{st}}\) of June every year since 2015.
To promote Yoga, Green park society in Pune organised a 7-day Yoga camp in their society. The number of people of different age groups who enrolled for this camp is given as follows :

| **Age Group** | 15 – 25 | 25 – 35 | 35 – 45 | 45 – 55 | 55 – 65 | 65 – 75 | 75 – 85 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Number of People** | 8 | 10 | 15 | 25 | 40 | 24 | 18 |

Based on the above, find the following :
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - a silhouette photograph of a person in a yoga pose; every number is in the table. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
Form the cumulative frequencies:

| Age Group | Number of people (f) | cf |
|---|---|---|
| 15 – 25 | 8 | 8 |
| 25 – 35 | 10 | 18 |
| 35 – 45 | 15 | 33 |
| 45 – 55 | 25 | 58 |
| 55 – 65 | 40 | 98 |
| 65 – 75 | 24 | 122 |
| 75 – 85 | 18 | 140 |

\(N = 140\), so \(\dfrac{N}{2} = 70\). The first cumulative frequency above 70 is 98, so the median class is 55 to 65.

Here \(l = 55\), \(f = 40\), \(cf = 58\) (the cumulative frequency of the class before it) and \(h = 10\).

\(\text{Median} = l + \dfrac{\frac{N}{2} - cf}{f} \times h = 55 + \dfrac{70 - 58}{40} \times 10 = 55 + 3 = 58\).

The median age is 58 years.

rows.subtopic: Mean of Grouped Data
rows.stem: If \(x\) more people of age group 65 – 75 had enrolled for the camp, the mean age would have been 58. Find the value of \(x\).
rows.context:
Yoga is an ancient practice which is a form of meditation and exercise. By practising yoga, we not even make our body healthy but also achieve inner peace and calmness. The International Yoga Day is celebrated on \(21^{\text{st}}\) of June every year since 2015.
To promote Yoga, Green park society in Pune organised a 7-day Yoga camp in their society. The number of people of different age groups who enrolled for this camp is given as follows :

| **Age Group** | 15 – 25 | 25 – 35 | 35 – 45 | 45 – 55 | 55 – 65 | 65 – 75 | 75 – 85 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Number of People** | 8 | 10 | 15 | 25 | 40 | 24 | 18 |

Based on the above, find the following :
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - a silhouette photograph of a person in a yoga pose; every number is in the table. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
Take the class marks \(x_i\) and form \(f_i x_i\):

| Age Group | \(x_i\) | \(f_i\) | \(f_i x_i\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 – 25 | 20 | 8 | 160 |
| 25 – 35 | 30 | 10 | 300 |
| 35 – 45 | 40 | 15 | 600 |
| 45 – 55 | 50 | 25 | 1250 |
| 55 – 65 | 60 | 40 | 2400 |
| 65 – 75 | 70 | 24 | 1680 |
| 75 – 85 | 80 | 18 | 1440 |
| Total | | 140 | 7830 |

With x more people in the 65 to 75 group, \(\sum f_i\) becomes \(140 + x\) and \(\sum f_i x_i\) becomes \(7830 + 70x\).

\(\dfrac{7830 + 70x}{140 + x} = 58\)

\(7830 + 70x = 8120 + 58x\)

\(12x = 290\), so \(x = \dfrac{290}{12} = \dfrac{145}{6} \approx 24.17\).

This is not a whole number, so as printed the data cannot give a mean of exactly 58: 24 more people give a mean of about 57.99 and 25 more give about 58.06. CBSE printed no solution for this part and awarded the full 2 marks to every student who attempted it.

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: The internal radius of hemispherical bowl (filled completely with water) in I is 9 cm and radius and height of cylindrical jar in II is 1.5 cm and 4 cm respectively. If the hemispherical bowl is to be emptied in cylindrical jars, then how many cylindrical jars are required ?
rows.context:
Khurja is a city in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh famous for the pottery. Khurja pottery is traditional Indian pottery work which has attracted Indians as well as foreigners with a variety of tea-sets, crockery and ceramic tile works. A huge portion of the ceramics used in the country is supplied by Khurja and is also referred as ‘The Ceramic Town’.
One of the private schools of Bulandshahr organised an Educational Tour for class 10 students to Khurja. Students were very excited about the trip. Following are the few pottery objects of Khurja.

Students found the shapes of the objects very interesting and they could easily relate them with mathematical shapes viz sphere, hemisphere, cylinder etc. Maths teacher who was accompanying the students asked following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - two photographs of Khurja pottery above a line drawing of the two shapes labelled I and II; the part names each object by its shape as well as its label, so it is answerable from the text. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
The jar is a cylinder with \(r = 1.5 = \dfrac{3}{2}\) cm and \(h = 4\) cm:

\(\text{Volume of one jar} = \pi r^2 h = \pi \times (1.5)^2 \times 4 = 9\pi\ \text{cm}^3\).

The bowl is a hemisphere of radius \(R = 9\) cm:

\(\text{Volume of water} = \dfrac{2}{3}\pi R^3 = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \pi \times 9^3 = 486\pi\ \text{cm}^3\).

Let n jars be needed: \(n \times \pi \times (1.5)^2 \times 4 = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \pi \times 9^3\), so

\(n = \dfrac{9 \times 9 \times 9 \times 2}{4 \times 1.5 \times 1.5 \times 3} = \dfrac{486\pi}{9\pi} = 54\).

54 cylindrical jars are required.

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: If in the cylindrical jar full of water, a conical funnel of same height and same diameter is immersed, then how much water will flow out of the jar ?
rows.context:
Khurja is a city in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh famous for the pottery. Khurja pottery is traditional Indian pottery work which has attracted Indians as well as foreigners with a variety of tea-sets, crockery and ceramic tile works. A huge portion of the ceramics used in the country is supplied by Khurja and is also referred as ‘The Ceramic Town’.
One of the private schools of Bulandshahr organised an Educational Tour for class 10 students to Khurja. Students were very excited about the trip. Following are the few pottery objects of Khurja.

Students found the shapes of the objects very interesting and they could easily relate them with mathematical shapes viz sphere, hemisphere, cylinder etc. Maths teacher who was accompanying the students asked following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - two photographs of Khurja pottery above a line drawing of the two shapes labelled I and II; this part is answerable from the text. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
The funnel is a cone with the same radius and height as the jar: \(r = \dfrac{3}{2}\) cm and \(h = 4\) cm. The water that flows out equals the volume of the cone.

\(\text{Volume of cone} = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{3}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{2} \times 4 = \dfrac{66}{7}\ \text{cm}^3\).

So \(\dfrac{66}{7}\ \text{cm}^3\), about \(9.43\ \text{cm}^3\), of water flows out of the jar.
